verdict.root_cause: Not established by the dispatches run. The investigation produced almost entirely empty answers: no change records for currency or flagd (and the change-log window queried started at the incident timestamp and ran forward, so the pre-incident period was never inspected) [tr_3b5b2c6af50d, tr_44946be55ff6, tr_3f0972f0bc05]; no span-metric samples for currency in either the incident or baseline window [tr_5c2870e93ffb]; no log lines at all for currency or checkout across the full window [tr_6277e4836179, tr_2bad76dcfe7d]. The only positive signal is tracing, which shows currency serving Convert normally in sub-2ms with no errors or timeouts, while the observed latency sits in cart's ~300ms Redis commands and in checkout self-time, with one truncated trace lacking its payment/email legs [tr_80287145255b]. That evidence actively exonerates currency as the origin despite triage starting there, but nothing dispatched examined cart, its Redis store, checkout, or the seven unmeasured edges, so the actual failing mechanism remains unidentified. The leading unconfirmed hypothesis is a slow dependency in the cart/Redis path dragging checkout and its fan-out of callers (payment, email, shipping, accounting, quote, fraud-detection) past their deadlines.
verdict.reasoning: Currency is ruled out as origin on the one dispatch that returned real data: its server spans are present, nested under checkout's client spans, and complete in 0.3-1.5ms with no error status [tr_80287145255b]. Its empty metrics and logs carry no evidential weight because the baseline windows are equally empty, which points at a label/pipeline gap rather than a failure at 23:50:31 [tr_5c2870e93ffb, tr_6277e4836179]. The same emptiness for checkout logs is systemic, not incident-shaped [tr_2bad76dcfe7d]. flagd shows error ratios at or below baseline and no recorded changes, so a flag flip is not supported [tr_30d3f3ec0d37, tr_44946be55ff6, tr_3f0972f0bc05] - though the change windows never covered the pre-incident hours, so a prior change is unexcluded. The only latency the traces localise is cart's Redis operations at ~300ms each and checkout self-time, which would plausibly propagate to every alerting caller [tr_80287145255b]; but the displayed traces are from 23:21-23:24, not 23:50:31, and are truncated, so this is a direction to investigate, not a finding. Naming a fault_class on this board would be invention.
open_questions: No dispatch examined cart or its Redis dependency, which is where the only observed latency sits - metrics, logs and traces for cart around 23:50:31 are needed.
The change-log window ran forward from the incident timestamp, so no pre-incident change for any service has actually been checked.

Were currency and checkout genuinely silent, or are their logs/metrics missing under a different service label? The baseline windows are equally empty, suggesting a telemetry gap that invalidates all absence-based conclusions.
No trace sampled at or after 23:50:31 was returned; the behaviour at the actual onset minute is unobserved.
Why did fraud-detection alert 60s after the others, and what do the seven unmeasured edges carry?

alternatives.root_cause: A slow or saturated Redis backing cart made checkout wait, and the wait propagated to every service in the checkout fan-out.
alternatives.why_not: The ~300ms Redis spans come from traces timestamped 23:21-23:24, half an hour before onset, and no cart-side metric, log or change was ever dispatched to confirm the condition persisted or worsened at 23:50:31.

alternatives.root_cause: checkout itself stalled - the trace showing ~620ms of PlaceOrder self-time with no downstream call and a truncated leg is consistent with checkout hanging and dragging its callers.
alternatives.why_not: A freeze would make checkout silent, but its logs are empty across the whole baseline window too, so the silence is a telemetry gap rather than evidence of a stopped process; and currency spans continue to be served as checkout's children.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric or log is expected. The observable that would justify a later proposal does not yet exist: the only latency actually seen in evidence sits in cart's ~300ms Redis commands and in checkout's ~620ms PlaceOrder self-time [tr_80287145255b], and neither cart nor its Redis store is a legal target in this blast radius. Nothing dispatched measured the service that would be acted upon.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a follow-up dispatch returns (a) a change-log query whose window actually precedes 2026-10-11T23:50:31 and shows a deploy or config/flag change on a service in the blast radius — which would meet rollback_image or revert_config preconditions, both currently unmet because every change window queried started at the incident timestamp and ran forward [tr_3b5b2c6af50d, tr_44946be55ff6, tr_3f0972f0bc05]; or (b) cart/Redis metrics and traces at 23:50:31 confirming the slow-dependency hypothesis, in which case the correct fix is restore_store or reconnect_service — both listed UNAVAILABLE, so it would still be outside what this system may do. Note also that the predicted effect of any restart here would be largely unobservable: currency and checkout return zero log lines and currency returns zero span-metric samples in both incident and baseline windows [tr_6277e4836179, tr_2bad76dcfe7d, tr_5c2870e93ffb], so an error ratio or log line 'ceasing' could not be distinguished from the pre-existing telemetry gap.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued customer-visible checkout latency across the seven alerting services while the cart/Redis path goes uninvestigated. Against that: the tempting action — restart_service on currency, where triage started — would recreate the one service that evidence actively exonerates, serving Convert in 0.3–1.5ms with no errors, no timeouts and no truncated children [tr_80287145255b]. That restart would discard currency's cache, add a cold-start latency spike on exactly the hop checkout depends on, and consume the incident's attention budget while the real mechanism keeps running. restart_service is also irreversible per the brief, and its precondition — evidence pointing at process state — is met by nothing on this board.
proposal.blast_radius: Unchanged by this proposal. For the record, had currency been restarted, checkout is its sole observed caller in the traces [tr_80287145255b] and would see connection resets, propagating to frontend and to the seven seed services that alerted (payment, email, shipping, accounting, quote, fraud-detection), turning a latency incident into an error incident.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Six services alerting simultaneously at critical severity with a seventh a minute later is a broad, undismissable failure. The simultaneity suggests a shared cause (deploy, config, or flag via flagd) but nothing yet distinguishes them.
